name: Oklahoma

law.summary: OPDES permits require reporting overflows and bypasses to DEQ (the federal 24-hour / 5-day condition, inferred). No duty to notify the public was found in the OAC 252:606 outline or by search; the relevant subchapters were not read in full.

citations.title: Subchapter 6 Point Source Discharges; Subchapter 11 Tests and Reports
citations.quote: (outline only; no section titled on overflows or public notice)
citations.deadline: 24 hours oral, 5 days written (inferred from the federal condition)

bills_and_cases: Not searched in depth; no 2025-2026 overflow-notice bill found.

erule.notes: No Oklahoma rows in SOBE; DEQ's own intake not found.

statewide_feed.notes: No DEQ overflow list, map, dataset or GIS layer found; the DEQ ArcGIS server has discharger points but no events.

habs.program: Oklahoma Tourism and Recreation Department lake algae status (Check My OK Lake) under 74 O.S. 2301; Corps of Engineers Tulsa District lake advisories
habs.notes: Site unreachable on the day (503 / TLS).

barriers.what: No public-notice duty found and no public list of overflow reports; reports exist only in DEQ files.
Overflow reports would need an Oklahoma Open Records Act request to DEQ.

readiness.rationale: No statewide overflow feed, no SOBE rows, no CSOs and no city overflow pages found. Show plant outfalls, the rain caution and the plain statement; add lake algae advisories once Check My OK Lake can be reached.

owner_questions: File an Open Records Act request with DEQ for SSO reports to document the barrier?
Use Corps of Engineers lake algae advisories for Oklahoma reservoirs?
surprise: Oklahoma's DEQ publishes a rich ArcGIS server (dischargers, drinking-water intakes, 303(d) waters) but nothing at all on sewer overflows, and its own OPDES rule outline has no overflow section.
